transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Sanjay Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (Acme Head of ML); Jorge Martinez (Acme Platform); Lena Wu (Acme DS)

Summary: quick run through of the model comparison tests, discuss pinning, fallback and rollback approaches, agree next steps.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight, we have about 45 minutes. quick roll call?
00:07 Priya Rao: yep priya here, hi all.
00:09 Jorge Martinez: jorge, platform.
00:11 Lena Wu: lena here.
00:13 Alex Chen: great, sanjay and i will kick off with the model compari- comparison results, sanjay do you want to share screen?
00:20 Sanjay Patel: yeah i'll share my screen, uh heads up the spreadsheet has the p50/p95/p99 latencies, token costs, and the quality delta against your incumbent model. some of the names are the open catalog variants: redwood-alpha-1, rwd-alpha-q4, and a smaller llm called coral-lite, and then we included anthropic-2 and openai-gpt64 as baselines for reference. names might be a bit off from your notes.
00:42 Priya Rao: perfect. the main concern for us is cost per token at scale and keeping p95 under 400ms for the user-facing path.
00:50 Sanjay Patel: right, on that the quantized rwd-alpha-q4 hits much lower token cost, and p50 is super low, p95 hovers around 420ms on the host pool but on dedicated it drops to ~360ms with the same workload profile. the coral-lite is cheap but quality degraded on longer context prompts.
01:10 Lena Wu: we saw hallucination cases on coral-lite with our billing reconciliation prompts, so that rules it out for the reconciliation flow.
01:17 Alex Chen: okay so that leaves the rwd-alpha variants as the top candidates. question for priya: are you comfortable with a quantized model in prod if we have a canary and immediate fallback?
01:27 Priya Rao: maybe; we need the quality evals first. lena is running the eval set. if delta is within the 2% threshold then we can consider.
01:36 Lena Wu: i'm about halfway through. initial runs show a 1.6% drop on F1 for entity extraction in the long-form prompts, but for short queries it's neutral. i'll push the full report today.
01:48 Jorge Martinez: from infra side we need to understand pinning behavior. if we pin to rwd-alpha-q4 and there's a regression, how fast can we rollback? will we be able to pin at request-route level?
02:00 Sanjay Patel: yes you can pin at route level. rollout options: canary (percent traffic), A/B traffic split, or full pin. rollbacks are immediate — you can flip the route to previous pinned model or to a fallback family. we also support automatic fallback: if p95 exceeds threshold or error rate spikes, requests are routed to dedicated fallback model like rwd-alpha-1 (non-quantized) or to hosted openai if you have that configured.
02:22 Jorge Martinez: and what's the time to change? is it eventual or immediate?
02:25 Sanjay Patel: config changes are near-instant across the control plane, propagation to the serving layer is usually a few seconds to 30 seconds depending on region and cache TTLs. there is a short window where in-flight requests may complete on the old model.
02:37 Priya Rao: that sounds acceptable. for audit and compliance we also need an immutable log of model version changes tied to user and SSO. is that in the private offering?
02:48 Alex Chen: yes, the private control plane includes audit logs and we can integrate with your SSO/SAML for RBAC. even on hosted we surface change events and have audit trails, but for strict immutability you might choose our Private deployment.
03:02 Priya Rao: good. also encryption/KMS question: our legal asks that keys are customer-managed for any PII.
03:09 Sanjay Patel: we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have envelope encryption and offer bring-your-own-key in select tiers. i'll drop the security note in the thread.
03:19 Maya Lopez: i'll attach the security pack and SOC2 docs to the follow up.
03:22 Alex Chen: thanks maya. back to pinning — recommendation from sanjay was start with a 5% canary for rwd-alpha-q4 with automatic fallback to rwd-alpha-1 and increase to 25% over 48 hours if metrics look good.
03:35 Sanjay Patel: yep, and set guardrails: p95 < 400ms and error rate < 0.5% and quality regression < 2% on the eval set. if any trigger trips, rollout stops and auto-fallback fires.
03:48 Priya Rao: i like that. question: what about burst capacity? some days we have sudden peak traffic, can the dedicated pool burst?
03:56 Alex Chen: you can configure burst capacity for Dedicated with a soft cap; the other option is autoscaling policies we can tune. i'll include the burst pricing in the quote.
04:06 Jorge Martinez: on the metrics we need to capture token breakdown per route to map cost. is that available?
04:12 Sanjay Patel: yes console gives token-level cost, latency breakdown and per-route dashboards. you can also trace individual requests through to model selection.
04:20 Lena Wu: can we pin per prompt type? our app has three routes: reconciliation, customer chat, and admin tools. we want different models for recon vs chat.
04:29 Sanjay Patel: absolutely, routing is policy-driven. you can have per-route pinning and different fallback chains.
04:34 Priya Rao: perfect. any known regressions in rwd-alpha-q4 vs rwd-alpha-1 besides the small quality drop?
04:41 Sanjay Patel: the quantized path sometimes softens rare tokens leading to minor entity truncation in long contexts — that's what you saw on the reconciliation eval. that is model-architecture/quantization tradeoff not an infrastructure bug.
04:55 Lena Wu: so for reconciliation we probably need the non-quantized rwd-alpha-1 or to pin to rwd-alpha-q4 only for short queries.
05:03 Alex Chen: noted. next, fallback to external vendor: you also have OpenAI credits, yes?
05:08 Priya Rao: we have limited credits. we'd prefer to keep traffic internal to save cost but maybe as last-resort fallback.
05:14 Sanjay Patel: we can configure multi-tier fallback: first fallback to rwd-alpha-1, then to OpenAI if enabled. also we support a degraded response path that returns cached prefix for certain reconciliation calls to avoid hallucinations.
05:30 Jorge Martinez: latency on double-fallback will stack. need to map that in SLOs.
05:34 Alex Chen: agreed, we'll include estimated latency impact for fallback chains in the spreadsheet.
05:40 Priya Rao: on the benchmark numbers, some p95s on hosted were 480ms, which is above our 400ms target; on Dedicated it looked fine. do you have a sensitivity analysis on traffic shape?
05:52 Sanjay Patel: yes, the spreadsheet has two workload profiles: conversational (short queries, bursty) and reconciliation (longer contexts, steady). dedicated GPUs give you more consistent p95 due to reserved capacity. we'll mark which models meet p95 under each profile.
06:08 Lena Wu: also important: KV cache behavior — we saw mismatches calling it kv cash in the notes — how does caching affect cold-starts for long contexts?
06:18 Sanjay Patel: kv cache helps a lot for repeated prefixes; for reconciliation where history repeats it's a win. for varied long contexts cache hit rate is lower so p95 benefits are reduced. we'll include hit-rate assumptions in the spreadsheet.
06:30 Priya Rao: ok. can you outline the exact canary plan in the doc? i want the steps spelled out.
06:36 Sanjay Patel: sure — step 1: provision dedicated pool and pin rwd-alpha-q4 for 5% of traffic at route-level; step 2: monitor p50/p95/error/quality metrics for 48 hours; step 3: if guardrails pass, increase to 25% over next 12-24 hours; step 4: if still good, full rollout. any trigger trips leads to immediate route flip to rwd-alpha-1 and an incident ticket.
07:00 Priya Rao: sounds good. who's owner of the rollout?
07:03 Alex Chen: we recommend a joint run with your platform lead (jorge) owning rollout and us standing by for rollback assistance.
07:11 Jorge Martinez: fine. we'll own it. need an exact runbook.
07:14 Maya Lopez: i'll draft a runbook and attach it.
07:18 Alex Chen: great. other concerns?
07:20 Priya Rao: SLA and SLOs. what's included in Dedicated contract vs Hosted?
07:24 Alex Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, hosted is best-effort with retention tiers. contract details in the quote.
07:31 Priya Rao: ok. one more question: can we pin to a model family with auto-upgrade when trusted? we want to avoid manual ops long-term.
07:39 Sanjay Patel: yes you can pin to family (e.g., rwd-alpha-stable) and set auto-upgrade policy: manual, automatic if regression < threshold, or scheduled upgrades. for POC we usually recommend manual or controlled auto with canary.
07:53 Priya Rao: we'll stick with manual for now.
07:55 Alex Chen: quickly on pricing — per-token for hosted, reserved commit for Dedicated plus lower per-token. alex to send numbers.
08:02 Priya Rao: thanks. lena will share full eval results later today?
08:06 Lena Wu: yes i'll upload them to the thread and flag any failing prompts.
08:10 Jorge Martinez: after we get the full eval we'll decide whether reconciliation route needs non-quantized pin and chat can use quantized.
08:18 Priya Rao: agreed. any blockers on our side?
08:22 Jorge Martinez: just procurement — we may need a PO for Dedicated. also legal wants the KMS note.
08:27 Alex Chen: i'll get procurement and legal docs over. maya to attach SOC2 and KMS options.
08:32 Maya Lopez: on it.
08:34 Alex Chen: ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
08:37 Alex Chen: recap: run canary 5% for rwd-alpha-q4 with guardrails p95<400ms, error<0.5%, quality<2% regression; fallback to rwd-alpha-1; Maya to share security docs; Alex to send pricing and burst options; Sanjay to share benchmark spreadsheet; Lena to finish evals. next meeting same time next week unless earlier.
08:58 Priya Rao: thanks everyone.
09:00 Alex Chen: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional ASR artifacts (product names sometimes shortened, KV cache as kv cash) and speaker labels are accurate but may be slightly off in a couple places.

References shared in call: link: shared-spreadsheet (model-benchmarks), link: security-pack.pdf, link: runbook-draft.md
